sentences.text:
1
 The Honourable Sri Justice K.Surender
 Criminal Revision Case No.1444 Of 2009
Judgment:

This Criminal Revision Case is filed by the petitioner aggrieved by the judgment dated 25.08.2009 in Crl.A.No.150 of 2007, on the file of Family-Cum-Additional Sessions Judge, Nalgonda,
confirming the judgment dated 29.11.2007 passed by the Judicial First Class Magistrate (Special Mobile Court), Nalgonda in C.C.No.38 of 2006.

entities.text: Judicial First Class Magistrate (Special Mobile Court), Nalgonda
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Learned counsel on record failed to appear on several occasions, for which reason, this Court appointed Sri Veluri Ravi Kumar, Retired District Judge as legal aid counsel.

3. Heard legal aid counsel and the learned Assistant Public Prosecutor appearing for respondent-State.
3.

The revision petitioner was convicted for the offense under Section 16(1)(a)(i) r/w.2(i)(a) and 7(i)
of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and sentenced to three months simple imprisonment and to pay fine of Rs.500/-.
The said conviction was confirmed by the appellate Court.
Questioning the order of the appellate Court, the revision petitioner is before this Court.
4. The case of P.W.1, who is the Food Inspector is that he was authorized to lift various food samples and accordingly on 23.11.2005, he went to shop premises of the revision petitioner.
While he was conducting business, P.W.1 found 3kgs. of laddu that was prepared and kept for sale.
On suspicion that the laddus would have been adulterated, he purchased 500 gms. of laddu and sent them to Public Analyst.
Formalities meant for sampling and other procedure was followed.
Thereafter, P.W.1 received the report of the Analyst, in which the opinion was given that sample do not confirm to the standards of maximum limit of permitted synthetic food colour.
Thereafter, notice was sent.
After following the due procedure, complaint was filed.
5. Both the Courts below found favour with the case of the Food Inspector that the there was adulterated colour used in preparation of laddus.
The said adulteration was that though synthetic food colour was permitted, it did not confirm to the prescribed standards of the colour used.

6. In the said circumstances, since the case is of the year, 2005 and nearly, 20 years have passed by,
this Court deems it appropriate to reduce the sentence of imprisonment to the period already undergone by the revision petitioner.
